assessed_fingerprint.rule: The first 16 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of a UTF-8 JSON text with sorted keys, non-ASCII characters unescaped and the separators ', ' and ': ' (Python's json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)). The value is an object with three keys, each holding a list of JSON arrays (not objects). records: for each record whose related_entities (not associated_entities) include one of the gap's entities, superseded records included, the array [evidence_id] followed by the values of record_fields in that order (null when absent), sorted by evidence_id. entities: for each of the gap's entities, [id] followed by the values of entity_fields (null when absent), sorted by id. relationships: for each relationship whose subject or object is one of the gap's entities, [subject, predicate, object, classification, evidence, note] with evidence in its ontology.json order and note null when absent, the arrays sorted by subject, then predicate, then object (unique, so later elements are never compared). Field values are copied as they are in the files, lists unsorted. A gap without entities has no digest.

checks.computed_relationships: Triggered when the computed list is empty.
checks.lifecycle_in: Triggered when a listed entity's lifecycle is not one of the check's stages; an entity without a lifecycle counts as not in them.
checks.no_ai_application_link: Triggered when any relationship, of any type and in either direction, joins the entity to an entity whose project_kind is ai-application.
checks.no_status_basis: Triggered when a record in the entity's lifecycle_evidence has a status_basis listed in the check's bases.
checks.rule: The checks and digests are in /data/gaps.json. A check type not listed here is an error, not a check to skip. A check holds when it is not triggered; a triggered check is an error only while the gap is open. An open gap must be re-assessed, and the build refuses to publish it, when a check is triggered, when its digest no longer matches, or when a record whose related_entities include one of its entities is missing from its assessed_records (whatever that record's dates).

derivation.computed_relationships: A gap with a computed_relationships check (list announcement_only) lists the matrix rows whose documentation_basis is announcement-or-description under the rules in /registry/matrix/matrix.json (derivation.documentation_basis), in the matrix's row order, each entry giving id, subject, relationship, object, classification, evidence (ids) and evidence_types (in the same order). Its count is stated as N of M: N is the length of relationships and M, published as formal_act_relationships, the number of matrix rows whose relationship type is a formal act. Every formal-act relationship type joins types inside the matrix's row selection, so these are all such relationships in ontology.json. The list measures documentation, not truth, and may include relationships already classified as announced plans.
derivation.entity_assessments: A gap with entity_assessments is assessed per entity, under the definitions in entity_assessment: one assessment per entity, in the gap's entity order, each listing the records cited for every dimension in the defined order. A cited record must exist, be a VERIFIED FACT and list the entity in related_entities. The dimensions are listed in dimension_order, the order in which they are displayed. An entity meets the operating path when operational_activity and outputs each cite a record, staffing or premises cites a record, and its lifecycle is pilot or operational; it meets the not_operating path when documented_non_operation cites a record and its lifecycle is discontinued. An entity is resolved exactly when it meets a path, with resolved_by listing records it cites; an open entity that meets a path, a resolved one that meets none, and a resolved gap with an open entity are errors. An empty list means no qualifying record is recorded in this registry, not that the thing does not exist.

dimensions.documented_non_operation: A record that the entity has ceased, been dissolved, or will not operate.
dimensions.governance_event: A meeting of a governing body, or the appointment of a named officer or board member.
dimensions.legal_approval: A legal act establishing the entity, such as a joint order approving its founding convention.
dimensions.operational_activity: Dated activity carried out by the entity itself: programmes run, calls launched, services delivered.
dimensions.outputs: Dated outputs of that activity: projects funded, people trained, systems or publications delivered.
dimensions.premises: Premises opened, occupied or in use.
dimensions.staffing: Staff recruited or in post, named or counted.

entity_assessment.note: A gap may assess each of its entities separately (entity_assessments). Each assessment lists, for every evidence dimension, the records that document it for that entity; an empty list means no qualifying record is recorded in this registry. An entity is resolved when its records meet one of the resolution paths below; it stays in the gap's scope, marked resolved, while other entities remain open. The gap is resolved only when every entity is.
entity_assessment.qualifying_records: A record cited under a dimension must be a VERIFIED FACT whose related_entities include the entity. Announced plans, targets and descriptions of intent do not qualify for any dimension.

resolution.not_operating: documented_non_operation cites at least one record and the entity's lifecycle is discontinued.
resolution.operating: operational_activity and outputs each cite at least one record, staffing or premises cites at least one record, and the entity's lifecycle is pilot or operational under the registry's status rules.
resolution.rule: A legal approval or a governance event never resolves an entity on its own. An entity marked resolved must meet a path and list the records that meet it in resolved_by; an entity that meets a path but is still marked open must be re-assessed.

established.text: The ministry presented Idarati AI as an agentic AI assistant for administrative procedures.
It was publicly available on the ministry's own services on 18 October 2026, and answered a test question through its public interface.

evidence_needed: An operator's report of use (annual report, parliamentary answer, published usage statistics)
An independent evaluation of the service
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: What documents actual use, adoption, accuracy, service outcomes or sustained operation of Idarati AI?
gaps.unestablished: How many people use it, its accuracy, its effect on administrative services, and whether it has operated continuously. Public availability on one date does not establish any of these.

established.text: The roadmap sets three 2030 targets: MAD 100 billion in added value to GDP, 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, and 200,000 trained and certified AI talents.

The ministry's September 2026 presentation of the roadmap's "main advances" restated the targets and listed items presented (the AI marketplace, Idarati AI, a proof of concept of a national meta-application and e-wallet), without quantified progress towards the targets.
Two projects are recorded as included in the roadmap, on the basis of that presentation.

evidence_needed: Official indicator reporting on the targets (ministry progress report, budget documents, national statistics)
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: What publicly documented measurements show progress toward the official targets of Morocco AI 2030?
gaps.unestablished: Any measured progress towards the value-added, jobs or talent targets. A project's status is not a measure of progress towards them.

established.text: Toubkal is listed in the June 2026 TOP500 as general-purpose high-performance computing; the listing documents capacity, not workloads or users.

A peer-reviewed article by authors affiliated with its host university states that large-language-model fine-tuning has been run on it, and presents as a benchmark the runs that produced the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija models.

The GemMaroc preprint that the article cites (Skiredj et al.; three of its five authors are from the host university) reports the hardware used, A100 GPUs and, for its largest model, eight H100 GPUs, and about 48 GPU-hours for that longest run, but does not say where the runs were made, and expresses their cost at a commercial cloud provider's public rate.
Two researchers of the host university report training a bacterial genomic language model on Toubkal: two A100 GPUs for 37 hours.

evidence_needed: Published usage or allocation reports for Toubkal (projects, GPU-hours, AI share)
Publications by authors not affiliated with UM6P that acknowledge Toubkal for specific AI models
A statement by the GemMaroc authors of where their fine-tuning runs were made
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: What independently documents AI workloads on the Toubkal supercomputer, and at what scale?
gaps.unestablished: Independent documentation of AI workloads on Toubkal, and the scale, share, users or continuity of its AI use. This is not a finding that Toubkal is not used for AI: researchers affiliated with its operator report specific runs. What is missing is documentation by a party independent of the operator, and system-level, quantified reporting.

established.text: Agreements on green data-centre infrastructure and on a data-centre partnership with UM6P were signed at the First National AI Conference.

The Nexus AI Factory memorandum was signed at GITEX Africa 2026 by Nexus Core Systems, the Ministry of Digital Transition and two other public bodies, according to the ministry's own release, which states its phase investment and capacity figures as commitments and documents no expenditure; the release does not reproduce the memorandum, and this registry has not obtained its text.
In April 2026 a convention that the ministry presents as following the green data-centres agreement launched the strategic studies for a green data-centre programme in Dakhla.

evidence_needed: Operator or independent confirmation that a facility is built and running
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: Which announced or signed computing and data-centre initiatives have verifiable construction, commissioning or operation?
gaps.unestablished: Construction, commissioning or operation of any of these facilities. A memorandum, a convention or the launch of studies is not construction.

evidence_needed: Published texts of the conventions and memoranda
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: Which relationships asserting a formal act (a signature, creation, designation, investment, development or operation) rest only on announcements, news reports or descriptions in this registry?
gaps.unestablished: Any record other than an announcement, news report or description for each relationship listed below. Relationships not listed cite at least one other kind of record, such as an official report or a technical repository. For eight signatures of the JAZARI ROOT and JAZARI Industrie X.0 conventions, that record is the Bulletin Officiel's publication of the conventions' approval by joint order, with a summary naming their parties; the other signatures not listed rest on an official report of the signing. Neither is the signed text, which this registry does not record for any signature. This measures how each relationship is documented in this registry, not whether it is true.

established.text: The strategy was launched in Rabat on 25 September 2024 by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform.

Its official 2030 objectives include 240,000 direct jobs with a contribution to GDP, digitalised public services, and a rise from 113th to 50th place worldwide on the ranking of online public services. The strategy's brochure defines that ranking as the United Nations Online Services Index (OSI), a component of the e-government development index (EGDI), and gives 113th as Morocco's 2022 position on it; the national news agency's dispatch calls it the e-government development index.

The Head of Government stated that public investment in digital technology rose from MAD 11 million in 2021 to more than MAD 1.7 billion in 2024. The registry has not checked these figures, and spending is an input, not a measure of the targets.
The ministry's report on the First National AI Conference frames the conference within the strategy.

On the overall e-government development index, the United Nations ranked Morocco 101st in 2022 and 90th in 2024. On the Online Services Index, its page gives Morocco's value (0.47210 in 2022, 0.56184 in 2024) but not its rank, so the strategy's 113th place for 2022 is the strategy's figure and has not been verified against a United Nations ranking. The 2024 edition, published in the year of the launch, measures the starting position, not progress under the strategy.

evidence_needed: Official indicator reporting on the targets (ministry progress report, budget documents, national statistics)
The United Nations ranking of countries on the Online Services Index, the index the ranking objective refers to, for 2022 and later editions
Finance-law documents for the stated investment figures
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: What publicly documented measurements show progress toward the official targets of Digital Morocco 2030?
gaps.unestablished: Any measured progress, after the strategy's launch, towards the jobs, GDP-contribution, public-services or online-services ranking objectives, and Morocco's rank on the Online Services Index in any edition. No project is recorded as included in the strategy, the investment figure is an unchecked statement about spending, and no edition of the United Nations survey later than 2024 had been published on the assessment date.

entities.name: Al Jazari Institute, Province of Nador

entity_assessments.note: A memorandum of understanding for the institute was signed on 2 July 2025 (MAI-EV-0005, MAI-EV-0019). No legal act establishing it is recorded in this registry; Bulletin Officiel 7534 contains none, which does not show that none exists.

established.text: The founding conventions of JAZARI ROOT, JAZARI EduTech, JAZARI Industrie X.0 and JAZARI Smart City were approved by joint orders published in Bulletin Officiel 7534 of 13 August 2026; the gazette publishes summaries of the conventions, not their signed texts.

The ministry states that the general assemblies of these four institutes were held in Rabat on 8 September 2026, chaired by the minister; the release names no director, board, budget, staff or premises.
A memorandum of understanding for an Al Jazari institute in the Province of Nador was signed on 2 July 2025.

evidence_needed: For each institute, records of staff or premises in use, together with dated activity carried out by the institute and its outputs, from the institute itself or from an official or independent source
Or, for an institute, a record that it has ceased or will not operate
For the Nador institute, the legal act establishing it, if one has been adopted
gaps.open_wording: No qualifying evidence is currently recorded in this registry.
gaps.question: Which JAZARI institutes have documented governance, staff, premises, operational activity or outputs, beyond their founding agreements and legal approval?
gaps.unestablished: For each institute: staff, premises in use, operational activity and its outputs, or a documented end of activity. For the Nador institute, also any legal act establishing it and any governance event. Legal approval, a general assembly, or a ministry's description of a move to operational implementation is not operation.

note: Open evidence questions. A gap records what this registry establishes and what it does not; it is a limit of the registry's coverage, not a finding that something does not exist. A gap is opened when a reference question asks something the records cannot answer; every strategy with an official target has a gap on its measured progress, which the build checks. Each gap stores the records it was assessed against and a digest of the data it rests on: when that data changes (a new or edited record, a changed stage, attribute or relationship), the build fails until the gap is re-assessed. Checks are re-run on every build against the canonical data.

states.open: The question cannot yet be answered from the records in this registry. It is a limit of coverage, not a finding that the evidence or the thing asked about does not exist.
states.resolved: Records in this registry now answer the question; resolved_by lists them.
